definitions.explanation: A polite way to ask about someone's identity.

examples.english: Who is it? / May I ask who you are?

examples.japanese: どなたかいらっしゃいますか。
こちらはどなたですか。
どなたか{日本語|にほんご}が{分|わ}かる{方|かた}はいますか。
examples.english: Is there anyone who understands Japanese?

examples.japanese: {先|さき}ほどお{電話|でんわ}をくださったのはどなたですか。
examples.english: Who was it that called earlier?

notes:
どなた is the polite equivalent of {誰|だれ} (who). It belongs to the ko-so-a-do demonstrative system and is used when politeness or respect is required.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
- {誰|だれ}: casual/neutral
- どなた: polite
- どちら{様|さま}: very polite/formal

COMMON PATTERNS:
- どなたですか: Who are you? / Who is it?
- どなたか: someone (polite indefinite)
- どなたでも: anyone at all (polite)
- どなた{様|さま}ですか: Who might you be? (very polite)

USAGE:
- At the door: どなたですか (Who is it?)
- Introducing someone: こちらはどなたですか (Who is this person?)
- Customer service: どなた{様|さま}がご{利用|りよう}ですか (Who will be using this?)

Part of the ko-so-a-do system: これ・それ・あれ・どれ, ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ, この・その・あの・どの, etc.
